correctness.rationale: Exact source coefficients give c0+c1=1 and Q=-γ(I-P). A direct stationary-projector computation derives x_t=(x0+tβ2x∞)/(1+tβ2), hence the full all-history, all-positive-t condition reduces equivalently to two endpoint-affine image conditions on [0,1]^2. Endpoint zero gives κ≥1/3; endpoint infinity gives (1+κ)^2(1-m)≤1; the latter implies the upper endpoint because m≤1/2. Explicit histories yield finite-time failures outside either bound. Intersection is nonempty exactly at m≥7/16; all strict/equality cases checked algebraically. The standalone exact-rational checker passed 2,637 comparisons, not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The criterion resolves an exact, motivated stochastic admissibility question for a contemporary optimized A-stable method under all positive steps and all valid two-history starts, not only an arbitrary special numerical instance. It yields a sharp stationary-balance cutoff m=7/16, equivalent max/min rate contrast 9/7, the unique boundary method and the entire admissible parameter interval. The exact stationary-projector interpolation mechanism distinguishes absolute stability from Markov simplex preservation, provides a reusable analytical benchmark for time-stepping probability laws, and highlights limits of broad absolute-monotonicity conditions; no general-dimensional or empirical significance is asserted.
